children: Anthropic's (ANTHRO) planned initial public offering is exposing a major vulnerability in its rapidly expanding AI business: nearly half its revenue depends on distribution through Amazon

Google. The concentration raises questions about the Claude maker's bargaining power, profitability and dependence on technology giants that are simultaneously its investors, infrastructure suppliers and competitors.

Anthropic develops the Claude family of AI models, competing with OpenAI and Google in consumer and enterprise AI. It generates revenue through subscriptions, usage-based API services and cloud marketplaces, where businesses can access its models through existing infrastructure providers.
According to its confidential IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters, Anthropic routed
47% of its 2025 sales, or approximately $2.16 billion
That dependence has grown rapidly. The two partners accounted for just 11% of Anthropic's revenue in 2023, climbing to 32% in 2024 before approaching half of sales last year.
The arrangement also carries a significant financial cost.
Anthropic paid Amazon and Google roughly
, equivalent to approximately 16 cents for every dollar generated through their cloud channels. Separately, the prospectus disclosed substantial revenue concentration among two unnamed customers.

The disclosures come as Anthropic prepares to enter public markets following extraordinary growth. Revenue surged twelvefold to approximately $4.6 billion in 2025, although operating losses exceeded $8 billion, according to Reuters.

For prospective Anthropic shareholders, the central question is whether rapid adoption translates into sustainable margins when a handful of companies control so much of its distribution and computing infrastructure.
Investors should monitor direct customer acquisition, cloud marketplace fees and whether revenue concentration declines as enterprise adoption broadens.
The relationship also has implications for Amazon and Alphabet, which benefit from Anthropic's expansion through infrastructure spending and distribution revenue.

With Anthropic reportedly targeting a valuation approaching $2 trillion, its eventual public disclosures on customer retention, partner economics and operating losses will be crucial to assessing whether its growth justifies that price tag.

title: Anthropic IPO Reveals Unexpected AI Industry Problem
